newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Gannet F field starts production - Shell.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Gannet F field starts production - Shell.

text.p: The Gannet F field in the central North Sea started production on Monday June 23, operator Shell UK Exploration and Production said on Thursday.
A Shell statement said peak production was expected to reach around 12,000 barrels per day (bpd) within a few weeks, adding the start came in under budget and two weeks ahead of schedule.
A Shell spokeswoman contacted by telephone did not give production volume on start-up but added that output volumes were building gradually upwards.

The development is part of a joint project which will see two new satellite fields, Gannet E and gannet F, exporting crude oil back to the existing Gannet Alpha platform, about 14 km and 11 km away respectively, through a common subsea pipeline system.
The Gannet Field is operated by Shell UK Exploration and Production on behalf of Shell UK Limited and Esso Exploration and Production UK Ltd.
The statement quoted Shell official Chris Finlayson, central field unit general manager, as saying:
"There is still a great deal of work to be done to maximise production from both fields but I congratulate everyone involved in the development for reaching this stage so successfully."
Shell said the field life is anticipated to be about 14 years with estimated recoverable reserves of 19 million barrels.
Oil from the Gannet E field will be brought to Gannet Alpha by the remote deployment of an electrical submersible pump in the Gannet E well.
